subject: Datacare DPA — ephemeral prompts, retention windows, and downstream model use
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@datacarehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@datacarehealth.com>, legal@datacarehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-14T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA clarifications — prompt retention and model use

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Legal had two follow-ups after reviewing the DPA:

1) We want to confirm how Redwood treats ephemeral prompts that contain PII. Specifically: what retention windows apply to prompt logs and associated KV caches, and whether those are ever used for model improvement.

2) We also need clarity on whether outputs (responses) derived from tenant prompts are considered "customer-owned" or if Redwood retains derivative rights for internal model improvement.

Our procurement timeline is tight — do you have a redline we can circulate that captures a no-training opt-out and concrete retention commitments?

Appreciate it,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Engineering Ops
Datacare Health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@datacarehealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — prompt retention and model use

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers first: yes, we can offer an explicit no-training opt-out for Datacare; we can also commit to a 30-day retention window for prompt logs by default (with options to shorten). Anything retained beyond 30 days is not used for general model improvement unless explicitly permitted.

I'll loop in Dev and Laura to propose precise contract language and to confirm the technical controls (ephemeral KV behavior, logs, export evidence). I'm attaching our initial redline for your legal team to review.

Next steps:
- Legal review of attached redline (Datacare_DPA_redline_v1.pdf)
- Tech notes: dataflow diagram and export-proof matrix for SOC/attestation
- If acceptable, we can hand this to Procurement for signature and DocuSign by end of next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Datacare_DPA_redline_v1.pdf
From: Legal Team <legal@datacarehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@datacarehealth.com>, procurement@datacarehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-16T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — prompt retention and model use

Marissa — thanks for the quick reply and the redline. A few detailed legal points we'd like to see clarified or tightened in the DPA redline:

- No-training opt-out: we need language that prevents any use of our prompts/responses for model training, tuning, or evaluation across all Redwood systems and subprocessor stacks unless we provide prior written consent.

- Subprocessors: include a requirement that any subprocessor receiving unredacted prompts must be listed in an appendix with region residency (EU/US/APAC), and that Datacare receives 30 days notice before any new subprocessor is engaged for processing of prompt data.

- Retention windows and deletion proofs: 30 days is a start; we'd prefer adjustable retention to 7 days for critical PII data. We need a mechanism to request proof of deletion (audit log or export) within 7 business days.

- Derivative/Output rights: Datacare requires that outputs generated from our prompts are owned by Datacare for downstream use, including embedding into our product, and that Redwood will not assert any proprietary rights over those outputs or license them for model improvement.

Could you confirm you can concede on the subprocessor notice and deletion-proof timing?

Regards,
Datacare Legal

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: legal@datacarehealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-17T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — prompt retention and model use

Hi Sanjay / Datacare Legal / Marissa — Jonas from Applied ML here. Quick technical clarifications to help align contract language:

- "No-training opt-out" scope: We can implement a tenant-level flag that prevents prompts, responses, or derived telemetry from being copied into our model training pipelines or shared feature stores. This flag also prevents automated retention-for-research workflows.

- Ephemeral KV and caches: For streaming and chat sessions we maintain an in-memory KV for active sessions; we can configure the system so that session KV is never persisted to disk for opted-out tenants. For non-opted tenants we keep session logs for up to 30 days.

- Shorter retention windows: We can support a 7-day retention policy for tenant logs with caveats: some audit logs required for incident investigation may be retained in hashed or redacted form for up to 90 days by default; however we can provide deletion proofs for raw prompt content within 7 business days on request (see attached export-proof-matrix.xlsx).

- Subprocessors and evidence: Any subprocessor that needs to access raw prompt content is currently limited and listed; we can provide a 30-day notice before onboarding additional subprocessors and include regional residency. Operationally, access is gated by KMS-based keys and HSM-backed vaults; we can provide attestations.

Suggested contract wording snippets for your counsel (short):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Data (including prompts and model outputs) to train, tune or improve machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent."
"Redwood shall delete raw prompt content associated with Customer within X business days upon request and provide a deletion confirmation or export log."

Happy to commit to work with legal to finalize precise timings and proof formats.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Research Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-18T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — prompt retention and model use

Hi all — following up with consolidated proposal after internal review. Highlights below and attached redline: Datacare_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (redline reflects agreed no-training opt-out language).

1) No-training opt-out: Redwood will implement a tenant-level no-training flag. Contract clause added: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data, including prompts and generated outputs, to train, tune, benchmark, or otherwise improve any machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent."

2) Retention windows: Default prompt retention = 30 days. Per-tenant option to set retention to 7 days for all raw prompt content. Audit logs required for security events will be retained in a redacted/hashed form for up to 90 days; raw prompt deletion requests will be processed and we will provide an export/deletion report within 7 business days.

3) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor appendix and agrees to 30 days advance notice before onboarding subprocessors that have access to raw prompt content. We will include region residency in the appendix.

4) Output/derivative rights: Clause added: "Customer retains ownership of outputs generated directly from Customer Data; Redwood will not assert proprietary rights or license those outputs for training or other commercial purposes without Customer's prior written consent."

Attachments for review: Datacare_DPA_redline_v1.pdf, dataflow-ephemeral-kv.png, export-proof-matrix.xlsx

If Datacare Legal can confirm acceptance of the deletion-proof timeline and subprocessor notice (both set to 7 business days / 30 days respectively), we can move to Procurement and DocuSign. Proposed next step: legal sign-off, then procurement signature by 2026-09-24.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if preferred.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
